pci_decision:
The latest information on record as per inspection Report, appeal/ compliance and AEBAS portal was placed and considered and following deficiencies are observed-

1. As per B.Pharm Regulations 2014 (Regulations 2014), 23 faculties are required. As per IR, 11 faculties were present for both D. Pharm and B. Pharm Courses combined. However, 0 (zero) faculties were verified on AEBAS Portal., attendance of 0 (zero) faculty were for last three months. Hence, appointment of these faculties appear to be non-regular faculties, not sufficient as per norms for introduction of new course.

2. Non-Teaching Staff Verification- As per Regulations 2014, 19 Non-Teaching Staff are required. However, as per IR 6 Non-Teaching Staff were present for both D. Pharm and B. Pharm Courses combined.

3. Lab Technician Verification- As per Regulations 2014, 5 lab Technician are required. However, as per IR 1 Lab Technician were present for both D. Pharm and B. Pharm Courses combined.

4. AEBAS Verification- Not Available

5. Appeal submitted does not rectify the deficiencies pointed

The institution is directed to submit the compliance within 14 days. Failure to comply shall amount to initiation of proceedings under Section 13.
With respect to other deficiencies, the Council will arrange inspection for verification throughout the year.

Note- Liability for Enrolled Batches: You are reminded that the administrative, financial, and legal liabilities concerning the protection, safety, and legitimate academic continuity of all enrolled batches rest entirely with your institutional management/authorities.

Further, with respect to the application for raise in intake, in view of the deficiencies observed and considering the information available on record, the institution was found to be substantially deficient. Accordingly, it was decided to reject the application for raise in intake in the B.Pharm course from 60 admissions to 100 admissions for the 2026–27 academic session.

The Pharmacy Council of India has taken note of the technical glitches in its 30.11.2023 because of which some institutions were conveyed rejection of approval for academic session 2023-24, though the conditional approval was granted already. The Pharmacy Council of India in its decision on 30.11.2023 has considered all pending applications with or without deficiency in terms of order dated 29.11.2023 of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Cont. Cas 1705 of 2023 and other connected matters whereby the Hon'ble Court had directed the Pharmacy Council of India to grant the approval to all institutions whose applications are pending for approval, though their deficiencies were communicated or not, subject to such institutions submitting an affidavit in 2 days with an undertaking to remove their respective deficiencies, if any, within a period of 7 days thereafter. The Pharmacy Council of India, therefore, on 30.11.023 has decided as under-

The institution is granted permission for the Academic Year 2023-24, however subject to the Principal of the Institution submitting an undertaking on an affidavit within 2 days to the effect that the deficiencies pointed out in the inspection stands rectified within a period of 7 days thereafter. If any deficiency found subsequently on inspection, the institution will not be considered for approval for 2024-2025 academic session.

institution_name: B.N. SINGH MEMORIAL HOSPITAL AND NURSING TRAINING INSTITUTE
pci_decision:
The latest information on record as per inspection Report, appeal/ compliance and AEBAS portal was placed and considered and following deficiencies are observed-

1. Faculty Verification- As per Education Regulation, 2020 (ER 2020), 7 faculties and 1 principal are required. As per IR, 8 faculties were present. However, 7 faculties were verified on AEBAS Portal., attendance of 7 faculty were not regular for last three months. Hence, appointment of these faculties appear to be non-regular faculties, not sufficient as per norms.

2. Non-Teaching Staff Verification- As per ER 2020, 16 Non-Teaching Staff are required. However, as per IR Details and designation mentioned in SIF of some non-teaching are not matching.

3. Lab Verification- As per ER 2020, 5 labs are required. However, as per IR shows that images of one lab is shown multiple times from multiple angles, the geo tagging of the labs is also not available. Hence, there is only 1 (one) Lab with temporary setup and very poorly maintained, hence not sufficient as per norms.

4. Classroom Verification- As per ER 2020, 2 classrooms are required. However, as per IR shows that images of one classroom shown multiple times from different angles without geo-tagging, hence not sufficient as per norms.

5. Equipment Verification- Deficient, not available as per norms.

6. AEBAS Verification- Not Available

7. Appeal submitted does not rectify the deficiencies pointed

The institution is directed to submit the compliance within 14 days. Failure to comply shall amount to initiation of proceedings under Section 13.
With respect to other deficiencies, the Council will arrange inspection for verification throughout the year.

Note- Liability for Enrolled Batches: You are reminded that the administrative, financial, and legal liabilities concerning the protection, safety, and legitimate academic continuity of all enrolled batches rest entirely with your institutional management/authorities.
examiningauthority_name: The Secretary Uttar Pradesh Board of Technical Education Guru Govind Marg Lucknow Uttar Pradesh

institution_name: CHIRAG COLLEGE OF PHARMACY
pci_decision:
The latest information on record as per inspection Report, appeal/ compliance and AEBAS portal was placed and considered and following deficiencies are observed-

1. Faculty Verification-As per Education Regulation, 2020 (ER 2020), 7 faculties and 1 principal are required. As per IR, only 3 faculty available without photo ID card and AEBAS, all faculties with no AEBAS registration and attendance data. Hence, appointment of these faculties appear to be non-regular faculties.

2. Lab Technician Verification- As per ER 2020, 2 lab Technician are required. However, as per IR, 0 (Zero) Lab Technicians were present.

3. Lab Verification- As per ER 2020, 5 labs are required. However, as per IR shows 6 labs with deficient infrastructure and equipments. Hence, Lab with temporary setup, hence not sufficient as per norms.

4. Non-Teaching Staff Verification- As per ER 2020, 16 Non-Teaching Staff are required. However, 5 were present.

5. Is Computer Laboratories Available As Per Norms- Not available as per norms, computer labs as temporary setup with laptops.

6. Equipment- Grossly deficient, Not available as per norms.

7. Is Social Pharmacy Laboratories Maintained As Per New Regulations- Not available, as per the image uploaded, temporary setup with some equipment shown.

8. Herbal garden- Not available as per image uploaded.

9. Smart Classroom- Not available, temporary setup with projector shown. No classroom available.

10. Model Pharmacy Laboratory Has Provision Of Drug Information Centre And Patient Counselling Centre- Not available.

11. Triple Door Entering Setup For Aseptic Room- Not available.

12. Bio Meteric Attendance System For Student- Not available.

13. Fuming Cub Board, Gas Fitting, Exhaust Fan- Not available.

14. Machine Are Fixed On Cemented Blocks- Not available.

15. No Of International Journals Available- Not available.

16. Is Display Of Chart In Respective Laboratories- Not available.

17. Appeal submitted does not rectify the deficiencies pointed

The institution is directed to submit the compliance within 14 days. Failure to comply shall amount to initiation of proceedings under Section 13.

Note- Liability for Enrolled Batches: You are reminded that the administrative, financial, and legal liabilities concerning the protection, safety, and legitimate academic continuity of all enrolled batches rest entirely with your institutional management/authorities.

pci_decision:
The latest information on record as per inspection Report, appeal/ compliance and AEBAS portal was placed and considered and following deficiencies are observed-

1. Faculty Verification-
As per Education Regulation, 2020 (ER 2020), 7 faculties and 1 principal are required. As per IR, 11 faculties were present. However, 0 (zero) faculties were verified on AEBAS Portal., attendance of 0 (zero) faculty were available for last three months. Hence, appointment of these faculties appear to be non-regular faculties, not sufficient as per norms for introduction of new course.

2. Non-Teaching Staff Verification- As per ER 2020, 16 Non-Teaching Staff are required. However, as per IR 6 Non-Teaching Staff were present.

3. Lab Technician Verification- As per ER 2020, 2 lab Technician are required. However, as per IR 1 Lab Technician was present.

4. AEBAS Verification- Not Available

5. Appeal submitted does not rectify the deficiencies pointed

The institution is directed to submit the compliance within 14 days. Failure to comply shall amount to initiation of proceedings under Section 13.
With respect to other deficiencies, the Council will arrange inspection for verification throughout the year.

Note- Liability for Enrolled Batches: You are reminded that the administrative, financial, and legal liabilities concerning the protection, safety, and legitimate academic continuity of all enrolled batches rest entirely with your institutional management/authorities.

pci_decision:
The latest information on record as per inspection Report, appeal/ compliance and AEBAS portal was placed and considered and following deficiencies are observed-

1. Faculty Verification-As per Education Regulation, 2020 (ER 2020), 7 faculties and 1 principal are required. As per IR, out of 7 faculties present, 2 are lab technicians, 3 having B. Pharm qualification with experience not as per norms, only 2 (Two) faculties with AEBAS registration and attendance data, other faculties are not registered on AEBAS. Hence, appointment of these faculties appear to be non-regular faculties, not sufficient as per norms.

2. Lab Verification- As per ER 2020, 4 labs are required. However, as per IR 4 Labs were shown photos of labs not proper, Inspector Remarks:- the number of equipment in some labs were not as per the requirement of PCI.

3. Equipment verification- Deficient as per norms.

4. Triple Door Entering Setup For Aseptic Room- not available.

5. Appeal submitted does not rectify the deficiencies pointed

The institution is directed to submit the compliance within 14 days. Failure to comply shall amount to initiation of proceedings under Section 13.
With respect to other deficiencies, the Council will arrange inspection for verification throughout the year.

Note- Liability for Enrolled Batches: You are reminded that the administrative, financial, and legal liabilities concerning the protection, safety, and legitimate academic continuity of all enrolled batches rest entirely with your institutional management/authorities.

institution_name: Spark College Of Pharmacy
pci_decision:
The latest information on record as per inspection Report, appeal/ compliance and AEBAS portal was placed and considered and following deficiencies are observed-

1. Faculty Verification- As per Education Regulation, 2020 (ER 2020), 7 faculties and 1 principal are required. As per IR, out of 28 faculties shown, 8 are lab technicians, 5 are having B. Pharm qualification with experience not as per norms, 1 professor with no AEBAS registration and attendance data. Hence, appointment of these faculties appear to be non-regular faculties, not sufficient as per norms.

2. Non-Teaching Staff Verification- As per ER 2020, 16 Non-Teaching Staff are required. However, 13 were present.

3. Lab Technician Verification- As per ER 2020, 2 lab Technician are required. However, as per IR 1 Lab Technician was present.

4. Appeal submitted does not rectify the deficiencies pointed

The institution is directed to submit the compliance within 14 days. Failure to comply shall amount to initiation of proceedings under Section 13.
With respect to other deficiencies, the Council will arrange inspection for verification throughout the year.

Note- Liability for Enrolled Batches: You are reminded that the administrative, financial, and legal liabilities concerning the protection, safety, and legitimate academic continuity of all enrolled batches rest entirely with your institutional management/authorities.

pci_decision:
The latest information on record as per inspection Report, appeal/ compliance and AEBAS portal was placed and considered and following deficiencies are observed-

1. Faculty Verification-As per Education Regulation, 2020 (ER 2020), 7 faculties and 1 principal are required. As per IR, out of 28 faculties shown, 6 are lab technicians, 1 having B. Pharm qualification with experience not as per norms, 23 faculties with no AEBAS registration and attendance data. Hence, appointment of these faculties appear to be non-regular faculties.

2. Lab Technician Verification- As per ER 2020, 2 lab Technician are required. However, as per IR 1 Lab Technician was present.

3. Appeal submitted does not rectify the deficiencies pointed

The institution is directed to submit the compliance within 14 days. Failure to comply shall amount to initiation of proceedings under Section 13.
With respect to other deficiencies, the Council will arrange inspection for verification throughout the year.

Note- Liability for Enrolled Batches: You are reminded that the administrative, financial, and legal liabilities concerning the protection, safety, and legitimate academic continuity of all enrolled batches rest entirely with your institutional management/authorities.

3. Lab Technician Verification- As per ER 2020, 2 lab Technician are required. However, as per IR 1 Lab Technician were present.

4. Lab Verification- As per ER 2020, 5 labs are required. However, as per IR 2 Labs were available.

pci_decision:
The Pharmacy Council of India has taken note of the technical glitches in its 30.11.2023 because of which some institutions were conveyed rejection of approval for academic session 2023-24, though the conditional approval was granted already. The Pharmacy Council of India in its decision on 30.11.2023 has considered all pending applications with or without deficiency in terms of order dated 29.11.2023 of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Cont. Cas 1705 of 2023 and other connected matters whereby the Hon'ble Court had directed the Pharmacy Council of India to grant the approval to all institutions whose applications are pending for approval, though their deficiencies were communicated or not, subject to such institutions submitting an affidavit in 2 days with an undertaking to remove their respective deficiencies, if any, within a period of 7 days thereafter. The Pharmacy Council of India, therefore, on 30.11.023 has decided as under-

The institution is granted permission for the Academic Year 2023-24, however subject to the Principal of the Institution submitting an undertaking on an affidavit within 2 days to the effect that the deficiencies pointed out in the inspection stands rectified within a period of 7 days thereafter. If any deficiency found subsequently on inspection, the institution will not be considered for approval for 2024-2025 academic session.

The Pharmacy Council of India has taken note of the technical glitches in its 30.11.2023 because of which some institutions were conveyed rejection of approval for D.Pharm & B.Pharm course for academic session 2023-24, though the conditional approval was granted already.

The Pharmacy Council of India in its decision on 30.11.2023 has considered all pending applications with or without deficiency in terms of order dated 29.11.2023 of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Cont. Case 1705 of 2023 and other connected matters whereby the Hon'ble Court had directed the Pharmacy Council of India to grant the approval to all institutions whose applications are pending for approval, though their deficiencies were communicated or not, subject to such institutions submitting an affidavit in 2 days with an undertaking to remove their respective deficiencies, if any, within a period of 7 days thereafter.

The Pharmacy Council of India, therefore, on 30.11.2023 has decided as under The institution is granted permission for the Academic Year 2023-24, however subject to the Principal of the Institution submitting an undertaking on an affidavit within 2 days to the effect that the deficiencies pointed out in the inspection stands rectified within a period of 7 days thereafter

The Pharmacy Council of India in its decision on 30.11.2023 has considered all pending applications with or without deficiency in terms of order dated 29.11.2023 of  Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Cont. Case 1705 of 2023 and other connected matters whereby the Hon'ble Court had directed the Pharmacy Council of India to grant the approval to all institutions whose applications are pending for approval, though their deficiencies were communicated or not, subject to such institutions submitting an affidavit in 2 days with an undertaking to remove their respective deficiencies, if any, within a period of 7 days thereafter.

The Pharmacy Council of India has taken note of the
technical glitches in its 30.11.2023 because of which
some institutions were conveyed rejection of approval
for D. Pharm course for academic session 2023-24,
though the conditional approval was granted already.

The Pharmacy Council of India in its decision on
30.11.2023 has considered all pending applications
with or without deficiency in terms of order dated
29.11.2023 of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Cont. Case
1705 of 2023 and other connected matters whereby
the Hon'ble Court had directed the Pharmacy Council
of India to grant the approval to all institutions whose
applications are pending for approval, though their
deficiencies were communicated or not, subject to
such institutions submitting an affidavit in 2 days with
an undertaking to remove their respective
deficiencies, if any, within a period of 7 days thereafter.

The Pharmacy Council of India, therefore, on
30.11.2023 has decided as under The institution is granted permission for the Academic
Year 2023-24, however subject to the Principal of the
Institution submitting an undertaking on an affidavit
within 2 days to the effect that the deficiencies
pointed out in the inspection stands rectified within a
period of 7 days thereafter.

The Pharmacy Council of India has taken note of the
technical glitches in its 30.11.2023 because of which
some institutions were conveyed rejection of approval
for D. Pharm course for academic session 2023-24,
though the conditional approval was granted already.

The Pharmacy Council of India in its decision on
30.11.2023 has considered all pending applications
with or without deficiency in terms of order dated
29.11.2023 of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Cont. Case
1705 of 2023 and other connected matters whereby
the Hon'ble Court had directed the Pharmacy Council
of India to grant the approval to all institutions whose
applications are pending for approval, though their
deficiencies were communicated or not, subject to
such institutions submitting an affidavit in 2 days with
an undertaking to remove their respective
deficiencies, if any, within a period of 7 days thereafter.

The Pharmacy Council of India, therefore, on
30.11.2023 has decided as under The institution is granted permission for the Academic
Year 2023-24, however subject to the Principal of the
Institution submitting an undertaking on an affidavit
within 2 days to the effect that the deficiencies
pointed out in the inspection stands rectified within a
period of 7 days thereafter.

 1. Principal and Faculty members were not present during online verification.
2. No joining and experience letter for Principal.

Deficiencies:

2.	Institute failed to produce sufficient document like degree and experience certificates.

3.	Principal documents like NOC and salary certificate were not available.

4.	Machine room was not as per norms.

5.	Social pharmacy lab is not available.

6.	CA Certified bills were not available.

7.	Electric points and Drainage and working benches were not proper as per norms.

8.	No preparation room in laboratories.

The Pharmacy Council of India has taken note of the technical glitches in its 30.11.2023 because of which some institutions were conveyed rejection of approval for D.Pharm & B.Pharm course for academic session 2023-24, though the conditional approval was granted already.

The Pharmacy Council of India in its decision on 30.11.2023 has considered all pending applications with or without deficiency in terms of order dated 29.11.2023 of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Cont. Case 1705 of 2023 and other connected matters whereby the Hon'ble Court had directed the Pharmacy Council of India to grant the approval to all institutions whose applications are pending for approval, though their deficiencies were communicated or not, subject to such institutions submitting an affidavit in 2 days with an undertaking to remove their respective deficiencies, if any, within a period of 7 days thereafter.

The Pharmacy Council of India, therefore, on 30.11.2023 has decided as under The institution is granted permission for the Academic Year 2023-24, however subject to the Principal of the Institution submitting an undertaking on an affidavit within 2 days to the effect that the deficiencies pointed out in the inspection stands rectified within a period of 7 days thereafter

institution_name: GATE COLLEGE OF PHARMACY
pci_decision:
The latest information on record as per inspection Report, appeal/ compliance and AEBAS portal was placed and considered and following deficiencies are observed-

1. As per B.Pharm Regulations 2014 (Regulations 2014), 23 faculties are required. As per IR, 23 faculties were present for both D. Pharm and B. Pharm Courses combined, out of which 3 are with B. Pharm Qualification with experience not as per norms. However, only 7 faculties were verified on AEBAS Portal, Hence, appointment of these faculties appear to be non-regular faculties, not sufficient as per norms for raise in admission.

2. Non-Teaching Staff Verification- As per Regulations 2014, 19 Non-Teaching Staff are required. However, as per IR 10 Non-Teaching Staff were present for both D. Pharm and B. Pharm Courses combined.

3. Lab Technician Verification- As per Regulations 2014, 5 lab Technician are required. However, as per IR 3 Lab Technician were present for both D. Pharm and B. Pharm Courses combined.

4. AEBAS Verification- Not Available

5. Appeal submitted does not rectify the deficiencies pointed

The institution is directed to submit the compliance within 14 days. Failure to comply shall amount to initiation of proceedings under Section 13.
With respect to other deficiencies, the Council will arrange inspection for verification throughout the year.

Note- Liability for Enrolled Batches: You are reminded that the administrative, financial, and legal liabilities concerning the protection, safety, and legitimate academic continuity of all enrolled batches rest entirely with your institutional management/authorities.

Further, with respect to the application for raise in intake, in view of the deficiencies observed and considering the information available on record, the institution was found to be substantially deficient. Accordingly, it was decided to reject the application for raise in intake in the B.Pharm course from 60 admissions to 100 admissions for the 2026–27 academic session.

"The Pharmacy Council of India has taken note of the technical glitches in its 30.11.2023 because of which some institutions were conveyed rejection of approval for D.Pharm course for academic session 2023-24, though the conditional approval was granted already.

The Pharmacy Council of India in its decision on 30.11.2023 has considered all pending applications with or without deficiency in terms of order dated 29.11.2023 of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Cont. Cas 1705 of 2023 and other connected matters whereby the Hon'ble Court had directed the Pharmacy Council of India to grant the approval to all institutions whose applications are pending for approval, though their deficiencies were communicated or not, subject to such institutions submitting an affidavit in 2 days with an undertaking to remove their respective deficiencies, if any, within a period of 7 days thereafter.

The Pharmacy Council of India, therefore, on 30.11.023 has decided as under-
The institution is granted permission for the Academic Year 2023-24, however  subject to the Principal of the Institution submitting an undertaking on an affidavit within 2 days to the effect  that the deficiencies pointed out in the inspection  stands rectified within a period of 7 days thereafter.

1. The principal was Anshul sharma with less experience for B.Pharmacy college. 
2. Faculties were absent and their consent were not verified.
3. Geo tag photos were not provided.  4. CA certified bill 

B.Pharm
Grant approval for 2023-2024 academic session for 60
admissions for the conduct of 1 st year B.Pharm course
"

institution_name: Mind Power College of Pharmacy
pci_decision:
The latest information on record as per inspection Report, appeal/ compliance and AEBAS portal was placed and considered and following deficiencies are observed-

1. As per B.Pharm Regulations 2014 (Regulations 2014), 23 faculties are required. As per IR, 6 faculties were present for both D. Pharm and B. Pharm Courses combined. However, zero (0) faculties were verified on AEBAS Portal., attendance of zero (0) faculty were for last three months. Hence, appointment of these faculties appear to be non-regular faculties.

2. Non-Teaching Staff Verification- As per Regulations 2014, 19 Non-Teaching Staff are required. However, as per IR 7 Non-Teaching Staff were present for both D. Pharm and B. Pharm Courses combined.

3. Lab Technician Verification- As per Regulations 2014, 5 lab Technician are required. However, as per IR 6 Lab Technician were present for both D. Pharm and B. Pharm Courses combined.

4. Lab Verification- As per Regulations 2014, 8 labs are required. However, as per IR 9 Labs were available for both D. Pharm and B. Pharm Courses combined.

5. AEBAS Verification- Not Available

6. Appeal submitted does not rectify the deficiencies pointed

The institution is directed to submit the compliance within 14 days. Failure to comply shall amount to initiation of proceedings under Section 13.
With respect to other deficiencies, the Council will arrange inspection for verification throughout the year.

Note- *Liability for Enrolled Batches: * You are reminded that the administrative, financial, and legal liabilities concerning the protection, safety, and legitimate academic continuity of all enrolled batches rest entirely with your institutional management/authorities.

pci_decision:
The Pharmacy Council of India has taken note of the technical glitches in its 30.11.2023 because of which some institutions were conveyed rejection of approval for  M.Pharm (Pharmaceutical Quality  Assurance),  M.Pharm (Pharmacognosy) & Pharm.D   course for academic session 2023-24, though the conditional approval was granted already.

Case 1705 of 2023 and other connected matters whereby the Hon'ble Court had directed the Pharmacy Council of India to grant the approval to all institutions whose applications are pending for approval, though their deficiencies were communicated or not, subject to such institutions submitting an affidavit in 2 days with an undertaking to remove their respective deficiencies, if any, within a period of 7 days thereafter.

institution_name: Baba Farid College Of Pharmacy Morkarma Mullanpur Distt Ludhianapunjab
pci_decision:
The Pharmacy Council of India has taken note of the
technical glitches in its 30.11.2023 because of which
some institutions were conveyed rejection of approval
for M. Pharm course for academic session 2023-24,
though the conditional approval was granted already.
The Pharmacy Council of India in its decision on
30.11.2023 has considered all pending applications
with or without deficiency in terms of order dated
29.11.2023 of Hon'ble Delhi High Courtin Cont. Case
1705 of 2023 and other connected matters whereby
the Hon'ble Court had directed the Pharmacy Council
of India to grant the approval to all institutions whose
applications are pending for approval, though their
deficiencies were communicated or not, subject to
such institutions submitting an affidavit in 2 days with
an undertaking to remove their respective
deficiencies, if any, within a period of 7 days thereafter.
The Pharmacy Council of India, therefore, on
30.11.2023 has decided as under The institution is granted permission for the Academic
Year 2023-24, however subject to the Principal of the
Institution submitting an undertaking on an affidavit
within 2 days to the effect that the deficiencies
pointed out in the inspection stands rectified within a
period of 7 days thereafter.
1. NOC for M. Pharmacy from state not available.
2. Structure stability certificate not issued by competent authority.
3. Qualified faculties are not available for M. Pharm in Pharmaceutical analysis at the time of inspection. 
4. Faculty cader ratio is not maintained.
5. Boy’s & Girl’s Common room is not available.
6. Microscope is not available at the time of inspection.
7. Only one lab has fuming board. 
8. Specialisation wise list of books are not available.
9. Photocopying machine is not available.
10. Internet facility is not available 
11. Licensed Plagiarism software is not available.
12. Audited financial statement of last three years are not available.
